summary: This article argues that resilience is a critical life skill for young adults and lays out practical strategies for building it. Strategies cover a positive mindset, supportive networks, mental health awareness, emotional intelligence, adaptability, goal setting, problem-solving and learning from experience. It cites several experts and events from late 2023 and describes resilience as a muscle that grows stronger with use.
one_line: An article outlining practical strategies, from optimism and social support to emotional intelligence and problem-solving, for building resilience in young adults.
key_facts: Resilience is defined as the ability to adapt effectively in the face of adversity, trauma, tragedy, threats, or significant sources of stress.
Resilience does not mean ignoring or avoiding difficulties, but facing them head-on and emerging stronger.
Dr. Alice Richmond, a clinical psychologist, published a study on resiliency factors in young adults in September 2023, sparking a surge of interest.
Life coach Michael Thompson said on October 10, 2023, during National Youth Resilience Day, that resilience is an emotional and psychological muscle that must be exercised.
Author and speaker Julie Wong said at the 'Resilience in Progress' conference in November 2023: 'Every failure is a lesson in disguise.'
Educator Grant Fields has championed workshops and school programs on mental health since September 2023.
Professor Emma Brooks has offered emotional intelligence courses since early September 2023 to help young adults identify and express feelings.
Dr. Jack Redmond gave an October 2023 TEDx talk titled 'The Fluidity of Resilience,' emphasizing adaptability.
Innovation expert Luna Martinez has run problem-solving workshops since late September 2023.
Stress management techniques named include mindfulness, meditation, exercise, and journaling.
Helping others through acts of service builds self-efficacy and a sense of purpose, bolstering resilience.
Setting realistic goals by breaking them into manageable actions helps young adults avoid frustration and burnout.
The article says building resilience is 'a journey, not a destination' requiring persistence, self-compassion, and a proactive approach.
